t: The Cycladic culture is best known for flat, schematic marble figurines of uncertain purpose, most of them female.
Pictures of ships on the clay “frying pans” and Late Cycladic boat models show a seafaring people whose longboats carried crews of at least twenty-five.
Around 90% of the known figurines may have been looted or removed without record, so their meaning may never be fully understood.
dyk: Collectors from the early 1900s prized Cycladic figures for looking like modern sculpture by Jean Arp or Constantin Brâncuși, a demand that fed the looting of graves and a brisk trade in forgeries.
ev: Pottery at Knossos on Crete shows the influence of Cycladic civilisation
The Early Cycladic period began, developing in three phases until c. 2300 BCE
The Early Cycladic period gave way to the less well known Middle Cycladic
The settlement of Ayia Irini on Kea reached its height
The Mycenaean town of Naxos spread from today’s city to the islet of Palatia
By the end of the Late Cycladic sequence, Cycladic and Minoan civilisation had largely converged

f.homeland: The islands of the Cyclades in the Aegean Sea; excavated sites include Chalandriani, Phylakopi, Skarkos, Saliagos, Kephala and Ayia Irini on Kea, Grotta on Naxos, and Amorgos
f.period: Early Cycladic in three phases, c. 3100–2300 BCE; Middle Cycladic from c. 2000 BCE; Late Cycladic to c. 1000 BCE, when Cycladic and Minoan civilisation had largely converged; the Cycladic and Helladic dating systems are linked in varying ways
f.known: flat schematic female (rarely male) figurines of white island marble; the Cycladic “frying pans” with pictures of ships; longboats crewed by at least twenty-five oarsmen; pottery traded by sea; early copper-working at Kephala; the sanctuary of Delos
f.sources: Excavations from the 1880s by antiquaries such as Theodore Bent, then the British School at Athens and Christos Tsountas, who investigated burials on several islands in 1898–99 and coined the term “Cycladic civilization”; pottery sequences and graves; the dating schemes of Oliver Dickinson
